description: baseline: lora_train.py as-is defaults (lora_r=256 q,v target modules, lr=2e-4, batch=16, context=full, no df), 10 epochs, best at epoch 7
exp01: baseline + --pos-weight (inverse-freq st2/st3 BCE reweighting), 10 epochs, best at epoch 9; adopting pos-weight as new standing default for future experiments

exp02: exp01 + lora_r 256->64 + target-modules query,value->query,key,value,dense (dense matches attn.output.dense AND FFN intermediate/output.dense, so this also LoRA-adapts the FFN -- confounds rank change with module coverage change, but net improvement is large). Note: ~7min/epoch (vs ~2min baseline) due to FFN LoRA adapters on 3072-dim matrices; adopting as new standing default

exp03: exp02 but attention-only (query,key,value,attention.output.dense, excludes FFN intermediate/output.dense) at same lora_r=64. Confirms FFN LoRA adapters are doing real work (0.588 vs exp02's 0.613), not just an rank-change artifact; back at ~2min/epoch though. Reverting to exp02 recipe as standing default

exp04: exp02 recipe with lora_r 64->32, STOPPED after epoch 7/10 (GPU needed elsewhere, not a crash) -- st3=0.523 already beats exp02's st3=0.503 at that point, so this could be competitive or better than exp02 if let run to completion; re-run to full 10 epochs when GPU is free rather than treating as a settled discard

exp04-rerun: same as above, run to full 10 epochs this time, best at epoch 7. Mean (0.604) is below exp02's 0.613, so r=64 stays the standing default -- but st3 is notably better here (0.529-0.536 across epochs 7-10 vs exp02's 0.503), dragged down by weaker st1 (0.618-0.630 vs exp02's 0.676). Worth revisiting r=32 if optimizing for st3 specifically

exp05: exp02 + st3-loss-weight 1.0->2.0 (upweight the weakest/most-imbalanced subtask's BCE loss). Big win: st3 0.503->0.602, st3_family 0.556->0.654, st1/st2 roughly held. Best at epoch 10 (still climbing at end of budget, not plateaued) -- new standing default

exp06: exp05 but st3-loss-weight 2.0->3.0. st3 keeps climbing (0.602->0.608, st3_family 0.654->0.668) but st1 drops (0.644->0.609) enough to lower the mean (0.631->0.622) -- 3.0 overshoots into hurting st1, reverting to st3-loss-weight=2.0 as standing default

exp07: exp05 recipe with lr 2e-4->3e-4 (curve was still climbing at epoch10 last time, hoped for faster convergence). Slightly worse (0.623 vs 0.631) and noticeably noisier epoch-to-epoch (st3 swings 0.336/0.519/0.476/0.511/0.470/0.563...), reverting to lr=2e-4

exp08: exp05 winning recipe with base model swapped roberta-base->legal-bert-base-uncased. KILLED by user after epoch 1/10 only -- far too early to judge (epoch1 numbers are always low/noisy, see baseline's own epoch1=0.319), inconclusive, re-run to completion later if domain-pretraining comparison is wanted

exp08-rerun: same config as exp08 (exp05 recipe on legal-bert-base-uncased), run to full 10 epochs this time (previous 2 attempts both cut short after epoch 1). Best at epoch 7 (mean_macro_f1=0.546), plateaus/wobbles epochs 7-10 (0.546/0.538/0.545/0.545). Clearly below roberta-base exp05 standing best (0.631) on every submetric -- st1 especially weak (0.585-0.604 vs roberta exp05 0.644) and st3 similar-ish (0.481-0.486 vs 0.602). Legal-domain pretraining does not help this task; reverting focus to roberta-base track

exp09: exp05 recipe (dense target modules, st3-loss-weight=2.0, pos-weight) with lora_r 64->32, run to full 10 epochs (revisiting exp04 territory per backlog). Best at epoch 9 (mean_macro_f1=0.625), epoch10=0.623. Close to exp05 (0.631) but still below it on mean; st3 (0.592) and st3_family (0.644) are close to exp05 (0.602/0.654) not clearly better this time, st2 is the best-yet (0.656). Confirms r=64 remains marginally ahead of r=32 when st3-loss-weight=2.0 is already applied -- the earlier st3 advantage for r=32 (exp04-rerun) does not clearly compound with the st3-loss-weight win. Reverting to r=64 (exp05) as standing default

exp10: exp05 recipe with lora_alpha 16->32 (r=64 unchanged, so effective LoRA scaling alpha/r goes 0.25->0.5). Best at epoch 10 (still climbing, not plateaued) -- new best mean (0.634 vs exp05 0.631). Tradeoff vs exp05: st1 up a lot (0.644->0.691, peaked 0.715 at epoch5) but st3/st3_family down (0.602->0.574, 0.654->0.636), st2 about flat. Noisier epoch-to-epoch than exp05 (st1 swings 0.539/0.590/0.619/0.645/0.715/0.625/0.616/0.611/0.666/0.691). Small net win, adopting alpha=32 as new standing default given it is still climbing at the epoch budget ceiling

exp11: exp10 recipe with lora_alpha 32->64 (r=64 unchanged, so alpha/r ratio 0.5->1.0). Strong new best, best at epoch 6 (mean_macro_f1=0.657, well above exp10 0.634 and exp05 0.631) then plateaus/wobbles epochs 7-10 (0.644/0.651/0.649/0.648) rather than still climbing -- unlike exp10 this one peaks mid-budget. All submetrics up vs exp05: st1 0.644->0.698, st2 0.648->0.662, st3 0.602->0.610, st3_family 0.654->0.663. Higher alpha/r ratio (stronger LoRA update scaling) is a clear win so far; adopting alpha=64 as new standing default, worth trying alpha=128 next to see if the pattern continues or overshoots

exp12: exp11 recipe with lora_alpha 64->128 (r=64 unchanged, alpha/r ratio 1.0->2.0). Another new best, best at epoch 7 (mean_macro_f1=0.668), st1 peaks 0.716-0.730 in epochs 7-10. All submetrics continue climbing vs exp11: st1 0.698->0.730, st2 0.662->0.665, st3 0.610->0.617(epoch6)/0.588-0.610 range, st3_family 0.663->0.678. Gains per alpha-doubling are shrinking (16->32: +0.003 baseline->exp10 is confounded by other changes; 32->64 exp10->exp11: +0.023; 64->128 exp11->exp12: +0.011), suggesting diminishing returns and a nearby ceiling. Adopting alpha=128 as new standing default, trying alpha=256 next to check whether the curve has peaked or keeps improving

exp13: exp12 recipe with lora_alpha 128->256 (alpha/r ratio 2.0->4.0). Clear overshoot: best mean_macro_f1=0.602 at epoch 10 (still climbing but far below exp12 0.668), st1 collapses to 0.588-0.640 range (vs exp12 0.693-0.730) while st2/st3/st3_family hold up better (st3_family even reaches 0.665, near-best). Too-large LoRA update scaling destabilizes st1 (the single-label softmax head) more than the multi-label sigmoid heads. Confirms alpha=128 is at or past the ceiling for this alpha sweep -- reverting to alpha=128 (exp12) as standing default

exp14: bisection between exp12 (alpha=128, 0.668) and exp13 (alpha=256, 0.602, overshoot) -- lora_alpha=192. Best at epoch 6 (mean_macro_f1=0.652) then wobbles down (0.625/0.632/0.617) before a late recovery to 0.646 at epoch10. Below exp12 on every submetric at their respective bests. Confirms alpha=128 is the local peak of this sweep (64: 0.657 < 128: 0.668 > 192: 0.652 > 256: 0.602) -- reverting to alpha=128 (exp12) as standing default and closing out the alpha sweep

exp15: exp12 recipe with lora_dropout 0.1->0.2 (more regularization on the alpha=128 adapters, hoping to smooth the epoch-to-epoch wobble). Best at epoch 6 (mean_macro_f1=0.637), below exp12 (0.668) throughout -- more dropout hurts rather than helps at this alpha, st3 particularly weak (0.489-0.572 vs exp12 0.588-0.617). Reverting to dropout=0.1, trying dropout=0.05 next (less regularization) as the other direction

exp16: exp12 recipe with lora_dropout 0.1->0.05 (less regularization, opposite direction from exp15). Best at epoch 8 (mean_macro_f1=0.640), still below exp12 (0.668). Interesting split: st3/st3_family hit new highs (0.642/0.688 at epoch10, best st3_family yet) but st1 collapses (0.605-0.655 vs exp12 0.68-0.73), dragging the mean down. Both dropout directions (0.05 here, 0.2 in exp15) underperform the default 0.1 -- dropout=0.1 confirmed optimal, reverting to it. Closing out dropout sweep

exp17: exp12 recipe with st3-loss-weight 2.0->1.5 (re-checking now that alpha=128 changes training dynamics a lot vs when 2.0 was originally chosen at alpha=16). Best at epoch 7 (mean_macro_f1=0.654), below exp12 (0.668) -- st3 clearly weaker at the lower weight (0.568 vs exp12 0.610) confirming 2.0 is still better than 1.5 even at alpha=128. Reverting to st3-loss-weight=2.0, trying 2.5 next as the other direction

exp18: exp12 recipe with st3-loss-weight 2.0->2.5 (other direction from exp17). Best at epoch 4 (mean_macro_f1=0.662), close to but still below exp12 (0.668). st2 notably weaker throughout (0.620-0.640 vs exp12 0.659-0.676) as the higher st3 weight pulls loss mass away from st2. Confirms st3-loss-weight=2.0 is the local optimum at alpha=128 too (1.5: 0.654 < 2.0: 0.668 > 2.5: 0.662) -- reverting to 2.0 and closing out this sweep. Standing best remains exp12 (r=64, alpha=128, dropout=0.1, dense target modules, st2w=1.0, st3w=2.0, pos-weight, lr=2e-4, mean=0.668)

exp19: exp12 recipe with lr 2e-4->1e-4 (hypothesis: alpha=128 already amplifies LoRA updates 2x, so halving lr might stabilize training). Wrong direction: best mean_macro_f1=0.624 at epoch8, well below exp12 (0.668) throughout -- convergence is simply too slow within the fixed 10-epoch budget (st1 never breaks 0.63 vs exp12s 0.68-0.73). alpha and lr do not substitute for each other the way hypothesized; reverting to lr=2e-4

exp20: exp12 recipe with st2-loss-weight 1.0->1.5 (st2 never explicitly upweighted before). Best at epoch 6 (mean_macro_f1=0.658), close to but still below exp12 (0.668) -- st2 does hit a new high (0.679 vs exp12 0.662) but st1/st3/st3_family all dip slightly, netting a small loss. Confirms st2-loss-weight=1.0 (i.e. leave it alone) remains optimal; reverting. Standing best remains exp12 (mean=0.668)

exp21: exp12 recipe with warmup_ratio 0.06->0.12 (hypothesis: more warmup would smooth the epoch-to-epoch st1 wobble seen at alpha=128). Best at epoch 9 (mean_macro_f1=0.633), well below exp12 (0.668) throughout -- st3/st3_family actually hit strong late highs (0.638/0.678) but st1 stays subdued (0.577-0.623 vs exp12 0.68-0.73), never recovering. Longer warmup just eats into the fixed 10-epoch budget without an offsetting stability win; reverting to warmup_ratio=0.06

exp22: exp12 recipe scaled up in capacity while holding the winning alpha/r=2.0 ratio fixed -- lora_r 64->128, lora_alpha 128->256. Best at epoch 9 (mean_macro_f1=0.644), below exp12 (0.668). st3/st3_family hit strong highs (0.629/0.686, best st3_family yet) but st1 is subdued and noisy (0.579-0.652, never reaching exp12s 0.68-0.73). More LoRA capacity at the same alpha/r ratio does not help and costs more compute (more trainable params); r=64 remains sufficient and preferred on the simplicity criterion. Reverting to r=64/alpha=128 (exp12) as standing default

last_layer-exp01: first real attempt at the src/last_layer track (frozen-encoder + N unfrozen trailing blocks, no LoRA/PEFT) -- the only prior log for this script used epochs=200/lr=2e-5/no-pos-weight and only reached 0.384 by epoch10, so this reconfigures within our 10-epoch budget: num-unfrozen-layers=3, lr=5e-5 (2.5x), pos-weight, st3-loss-weight=2.0 (borrowing the winning LoRA recipes insights). Best at epoch 9 (mean_macro_f1=0.638), close to but below LoRA exp12 (0.668). Notably much smoother/more monotonic epoch-to-epoch than the alpha=128 LoRA runs (no big st1 wobble) -- a genuinely competitive, simpler alternative architecture. Still below standing LoRA best so discard for now, but worth 1-2 more last_layer experiments (more unfrozen layers / higher lr) given it was still climbing at epoch 9

last_layer-exp02: last_layer-exp01 recipe with num-unfrozen-layers 3->6 (more capacity). Best at epoch 10 (mean_macro_f1=0.625), slightly worse than exp01 (0.638) and slower per-epoch (~87s vs ~70s, more unfrozen params). More unfrozen layers does not help within the 10-epoch budget -- 3 layers remains the better last_layer config. Confirms LoRA (exp12, 0.668) stays the stronger approach; last_layer is a viable simpler alternative topping out around 0.638 but not competitive with the tuned LoRA recipe. Deprioritizing further last_layer exploration, returning focus to the LoRA track

exp23: exp12 recipe but attention-only target-modules (query,key,value, dropping dense/FFN) to check whether the higher alpha=128 scaling narrows the gap seen back in exp03 (attention-only at alpha=16 got 0.588 vs exp02s 0.613 with dense). It does not: best mean_macro_f1=0.603 at epoch6, still far below exp12 (0.668) and barely above exp03s old alpha=16 result. FFN/dense LoRA adapters remain essential regardless of alpha -- closing this question, keeping dense in target-modules as a fixed part of the recipe going forward

exp24: exp12 recipe with batch_size 16->32 (half as many optimizer steps per epoch). Best at epoch 10 (mean_macro_f1=0.626, still climbing), below exp12 (0.668) throughout and noticeably slower wall-clock per epoch too (~2min vs ~75s, larger batches). Fewer steps per epoch hurts within the fixed 10-epoch budget even though per-step gradient estimates are less noisy; reverting to batch_size=16. Closing out the batch size probe -- standing best remains exp12 (r=64, alpha=128, dropout=0.1, dense target modules, st2w=1.0, st3w=2.0, pos-weight, lr=2e-4, batch=16, mean=0.668)

exp25: exp12 recipe plus new --head-lr flag (code change, committed at e849c71) giving the randomly-initialized st1/st2/st3 heads their own LR separate from the LoRA adapters -- head-lr=5e-4 (2.5x the base lr=2e-4), on the theory that from-scratch heads might want to move faster than LoRA nudges to a pretrained encoder. Best at epoch 7 (mean_macro_f1=0.655), close to but below exp12 (0.668). st1 hits a new high (0.720) but st3 dips (0.579) relative to exp12, netting a small loss. Single shared LR (previous behavior) remains at least as good; not adopting head-lr for now, though the flag stays available for future retries at other values
